chunks: And it is narrated from Ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Regarding a man who buys a غلام or a female slave, while he has a brother, sister, father, or mother in one of the cities, he said: "He should not take him out from one city to another city if he is young, nor should he buy him. But if he has a mother, and her nafs and his nafs are content, then buy him if you wish."

key_terms.أُمٌّ: the mother, whose consent is specifically considered
key_terms.صَغِيرًا: young in age, making removal and purchase restricted
key_terms.مِصْرٍ: a city or region from which the slave is not to be removed
key_terms.نَفْسُهَا: her willing acceptance or inner contentment
key_terms.نَفْسُهُ: his willing acceptance or inner contentment
key_terms.ٱلْجَارِيَةَ: a female slave included in the same legal ruling
key_terms.ٱلْغُلَامَ: a young male slave being discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Can a young slave be bought and moved away from a city when close family members live there?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the purchase and transfer of a young slave who has close family members residing in a city. It forbids removing such a child from that city or purchasing him, except where the mother and the child are both content with the sale.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3827 - Ibn Sinan narrated that Abu Abdullah (as) said:

"Regarding a man who buys a male or female slave, and the slave has a brother, sister, father, or mother in one of the cities, he should not take the slave out of that city to another city if the slave is young, nor should he buy him.
However, if the slave has a mother and both she and the slave are content with the sale, then he may buy the slave if he wishes."
